reviews.text: Hands down the very best veterinary clinic in San Antonio. Dr. Jasmine Riley is professional yet personable, kind, well versed and educated in her field. Our visit was excellent

Exceptional service!! They truly care about you and your fur baby. Dr Riley is so compassionate and listens to you and your concerns about what's going on with your fur baby.   She explains everything in detail and they handle your pet with the utmost care. All the techs were compassionate and knowledgeable as well. Very reasonable prices compared to other animal emergency hospitals (they don't gouge your eyes out) lol. I will definitely be bringing back my little Snowy girl to them. I trust them 100%. I even had to leave my cat over there for a couple of hours so they could get a urine sample from her since she had no pee in her bladder. Dr Riley called me as soon the lab work and urinalysis came in and gave me a complete treatment plan for her and went over what issues she was having and the prescriptions that I would need to administer and when. I am forever grateful to them. Thank you Dr Riley and team !!!❤️❤️❤️

I lost it. Not only did they not dose her with medication while there, the medication they did prescribe was another $$$$ and no diagnosis. Thinking they could guilt me in paying more. I left. It took a few days. Pumpkin baby food. My dog is happy and doing well.

I brought my 14 year old dog in last year during the summer in june . Braught her in for an x-ray because we thought she had something stuck in her system having trouble using the restroom. They charged me seven hundred and fifty dollars for an x ray . They took me in when it was done . They pointed at it and said, that's the biggest tumor we've ever seen in a little dog . The vet diagnosed her 6 days to 6 weeks of life expectancy and then she would have a quick death. They offered to euthanize my dog , or put her in hospice there and then euthanize her if needed. They also said they could do a biopsy for $5000.  I said I would do hospice . They sent me home with a variety of drugs . But they charged me thirty dollars over what a normal vet charges for a smaller bottle of painkiller for my dog. Long story short , it's february of 2026 and my dog did not die and is still alive . I've gone to another vet to continue treatment . If I were to left her with town north animal hospital she would be a dead dog today. What I do know is a fact is that they diagnose her as a dead dog walking . And I know for a fact that they overcharged me on painkiller, and I'm sure all the other drugs and services. If you want your dog or cat to be a Revenue Source,  by all means, take them to Town North Animal hospital . And if your dog's older like mine , I'm sure they'd be happy to kill them for you.

A Clinic That Became Home – A Tribute to a Lifetime of Care

Towne North Animal Hospital isn’t just a vet clinic to me—it’s where some of the most important companions of my life were seen, treated, and laid to rest. Junior. GMoney. A tiny pup who didn’t make it through parvo. Each of them walked through these doors—and were met with presence, patience, and love.

The doctor who led this clinic for decades (now retired) left an imprint you can still feel in the walls. He wasn’t just good—he was grounded. Gentle. Wise. You knew your animal mattered when he entered the room.

Even now, with new leadership, I feel the same care trying to carry forward. The space still feels sacred to me. The team continues that legacy—even if they don’t know the full weight of what they’ve inherited.

If you’re looking for flashy or fast, this may not be your place.

But if you’re looking for trust, heart, and real care—you’ve just found your sanctuary
